[2026-06-01 01:24] Excellent manifest — thorough and well-reasoned. Decisions on your three questions, then go:

1. **Prefix → `seasons_`** (your recommendation). It matches the module, spec, and plan; consistency with the code wins over retrofitting a never-used `events_` convention. Add a one-line note to `i18n-conventions.md` documenting `seasons_` as the events-domain sub-group for this slice.
2. **Shared field labels → keep under `seasons_field_*`** (your default). No premature hoist to `common_field_*`; we refactor if real cross-feature reuse emerges.
3. **`seasons_eyebrow` = "Season"** is fine as a static eyebrow label — Byrd will confirm during the Task 15 route whether the route uses it or the DB season name; if unused it's harmless. Keep it.

Also approved: single `seasons_error_outside_season` key (field-level targeting disambiguates); the `{n}` plural handling per the no-ICU-plural convention (your et/lv/uk partitive/genitive choices are sound). The partial-failure notices, page title, confirmations — all good.

**One accuracy check before you commit:** cross-reference your four `seasons_error_*` keys against the ACTUAL `code` strings emitted by `src/lib/seasons/validation.ts` (now GREEN at `6fdef24`) — not just the plan's Task 2 sketch. The keys must match the real codes (`blank`, `end_before_start`, `interval_too_small`, `outside_season` — confirm exact spelling) so Byrd can map `code → m.seasons_error_<code>()` cleanly.

**Then commit** the `seasons_*` set across all four locales (en real + et/lv/uk real translations, keys in sync) + the i18n-conventions.md note.

**Worktree + concurrency:** work in your own worktree at `origin/feat/rehearsal-schedule`. Josquin is committing `seasonsStore.ts` to the same branch in parallel — disjoint from your `messages/*.json`, so if your push is rejected (non-fast-forward), `git fetch && git rebase origin/feat/rehearsal-schedule` (clean) and push again. Handoff to me with tip SHA when committed — that unblocks Byrd's components.
summary: Manifest approved with decisions — create the keys
